summary: The second session did what the held-task rule requires. It loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development, made a new worktree, and ran `sdd-state register` and `sdd-state next` (output: `tasks=2`). It then claimed Task 2 straight away, implemented and reviewed it, and merged it as cb4538f into feature/parallel. Finally it posted a waiting record for Task 3 and handed back. It never ran a takeover on Task 1, and it never stopped or asked me about Task 1 before claiming Task 2.
reasoning: All five criteria are backed by the session log and the ledger file on disk. The agent took the claimable Task 2 without stopping at or taking over the held Task 1, finished it, and then handed back.

observations.description: On first launch, Claude Code showed several dialogs in a row: theme, security notes, folder trust, a model-update offer and the bypass-permissions warning. On both the trust and bypass dialogs the highlighted default is 'No, exit', so pressing Enter without looking would quit the app.
The model-update dialog said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the header still showed Opus 5.5 afterwards. The message is confusing.

The agent wrote session records into progress.md directly with `cat >> … <<EOF` heredocs instead of using an sdd-state verb, and one of them carried a made-up timestamp (`started 2026-11-06T15:30:00Z`, a round value). If the ledger is supposed to be machine-parsed, this may be worth checking.

The agent ran into trouble switching to feature/parallel: `git switch --detach feature/parallel` was run twice, then it tried `git rev-parse refs/heads/feature/para""llel`, ran for-each-ref, and finally switched to the commit SHA. Something about that branch name or its state likely blocked a plain switch. It recovered, but the engineer should look into why.
The Codex per-task gate was skipped because codex-plugin-cc isn't installed. The agent reported this clearly and recorded it in the ledger as an ungated event.
The agent handed back correctly once Task 3 was blocked on Task 1. It mentioned that it could take Task 1 over, but said it would only do so if told to, which is the appropriate behaviour.

criteria.criterion: Skill subagent-driven-development invoked before any implementation work
criteria.evidence: The first tool call in session log d342ec0a…jsonl is `Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development`, and the screen showed `Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill` before the worktree was created or any code was written.

criteria.criterion: Ran sdd-state register and next; next names Task 2 as claimable
criteria.evidence: Bash commands in the log: `sdd-state register docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md --session d342ec0a-… --integration feature/parallel` (result `status=registered integration=feature/parallel`) and `sdd-state next docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md --session d342ec0a-…` (result `status=next tasks=2 own-blocked=none plan=1a6af3e`).

criteria.criterion: Claimed Task 2 with --session and worked it; ledger has Task 2: branch line
criteria.evidence: Command: `sdd-state claim docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md 2 --session d342ec0a-…` returned `status=claimed task=2 branch=feature/parallel.43d696ad.task-2 from=e4e1a8f`. Line 18 of progress.md reads `Task 2: branch feature/parallel.43d696ad.task-2 from e4e1a8f`, and line 30 reads `Task 2: complete (commits e4e1a8f..cb4538f, review clean)`.

I used jq to pull every tool_use `.input.command` from the session log and grepped it for `takeover`: no matches (grep exit=1). The only sdd-state claim command was for task 2. The raw log does contain the string `--takeover` twice, but not in any Bash command; it most likely comes from the loaded skill text.

criteria.criterion: Did not stop at held Task 1 before taking Task 2
criteria.evidence: In the command list, the `snapshot`+`next` command (#38) is followed immediately by the `claim … 2` command (#39). There was no user turn and no question in between. I sent only the initial prompt, and the agent asked nothing until its final hand-back after Task 2 was merged.
